label: Game A
nuance_found: Handbrake into a corner for a drift multiplier, and flick the steering back and forth for a SWITCH bonus. Smashing lamp posts and bollards in a chain pays far more than clean driving, so going off the road on purpose scores well. Nothing I had to weigh against anything else.
audio: Procedural music loop from the start, tire and impact tones, rumble, and phone vibration on hits. It never went silent, but the music was a thin loop and the effects blurred together.
furthest_progress: Yozakura Pass, Easy: 38 mi, best score 11,249 at about 540 s (in-game clock 23:42, night with rain, through a tunnel and the golden hour, blue hour and night phases). Dawn never came.
control_trouble: Steering reads from how far my finger slides from where it went down, and I only see the screen every 0.5 s, so I overshot most bends and hit rails. I did not try to fix that with finer acts for most of the run. A real thumb would be better, but the road also bends fast at 80 to 100 mph with little warning, so some of this is the game.
best_moment: A clean handbrake drift through a bend at night, tire smoke and a multiplier popping up, then a lamp post smash for +1,000.
worst_moment: Going off the road, then sitting 6 to 8 seconds in the BACK TO THE ROAD magnet rescue with no control. It happened over and over, and a few times I got stuck against a guardrail with the car facing the wrong way.
verdict: It looks great and the first minute feels good: hold to drive, the car slides, things explode into points. But I spent about a third of my time off the road waiting for a giant magnet to lift my car back, and I kept pinning myself on a guardrail. The goal (drift to bring dawn closer) is not something I could really feel in ten minutes, since the clock just ticks. Smashing scenery paid more than driving well, which seems backwards. I would give it a few more tries on a long bus ride, but I would not tell anyone about it, and I probably delete it by tomorrow.
